transcript.content: Hi, welcome in — I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?
I came in because I can’t shake this heavy, hopeless feeling. Ever since the divorce, it feels like everything I worked to build has just collapsed, and I’m sitting under it.
When did the divorce happen, and how soon after that did you start noticing this heavy, hopeless feeling?
The divorce was before the financial mess really hit. The heavy, hopeless feeling has been hanging over me for about a month now, since all of that started.
Over this past month, have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, even when you're not thinking about the divorce or finances?
I’m not really sure. I know I’ve been feeling awful, but I haven’t really paid attention to whether it’s a loss of interest or just everything feeling so overwhelming.
Over this past month, have you noticed any changes in your sleep, like trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or sleeping much more than usual?
Yeah. Some nights I just lie there staring at the ceiling, replaying bills and mistakes I made at work. Other times I wake up before dawn and feel like I barely slept at all.
Over the past month, have you found yourself feeling worthless or excessively guilty about things, beyond just the stress of the divorce and finances?
Yes. I keep thinking I’m a terrible engineer, a failed wife, and just a burden to everyone. I replay every calculation I missed or tense email I sent like it proves I ruin things.
Over this past month, have you had any thoughts of death or of hurting yourself?
Yes. I’ve been thinking it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up. It got intense enough that it scared me, and I called the employee assistance program.
Have you ever had a period like this before—weeks or more of feeling this down, hopeless, or losing interest in things—at any other point earlier in your life, even years ago?
I’m not sure. I can’t really think of another time that lasted weeks like this.

Over this past month, how has this been affecting your ability to function day-to-day — for example, are you still able to go to work, manage daily tasks, and take care of yourself, or has it become very difficult to do those things?

It’s become very difficult. At work I was making questionable calls and falling apart in meetings, and my supervisor had to take me off active project decisions. At home I stopped keeping up with basic routines. It got bad enough that I was sent to the emergency department because I didn’t feel safe with my thoughts.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports a one-month period of pervasive depressed/hopeless mood following a divorce and financial crisis, accompanied by insomnia with early morning awakening, feelings of worthlessness and excessive guilt, active suicidal ideation requiring EAP contact and ED evaluation, and marked functional impairment at work (removed from active duties, poor performance) and at home (unable to maintain basic routines). This constellation meets criteria for a single major depressive episode of severe intensity without any reported psychotic features (no hallucinations or delusions elicited). Adjustment disorder (F43.21) was considered given the clear psychosocial stressor, but the severity, duration, number of symptoms (mood, sleep, guilt, suicidality, functional collapse), and presence of suicidal ideation exceed the threshold for adjustment disorder and meet full criteria for a severe depressive episode. No history of prior depressive or manic episodes was identified, supporting a single-episode designation rather than recurrent depressive disorder.
